name: Gumroad
tagline: Sell a few digital files through Stripe Checkout and a user-owned delivery page

pricing.notes: No fixed monthly fee; Gumroad charges transaction fees.

tiers.name: Creator account
tiers.limits: No published cap on products or revenue; direct/profile sales cost 10% + $0.50 plus processing.

pricing.freeTierCaps: No monthly fee and no published product/revenue cap; direct sales pay 10% + $0.50 plus payment processing
pricing.billingTerms: transaction-only pricing; no monthly or annual subscription
pricing.hiddenCosts: Direct/profile sales add payment processing (typically 2.9% + $0.30 for cards) to Gumroad's 10% + $0.50; Discover marketplace sales cost 30% including processing; processing fees are not returned on refunds.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Gumroad, sell a few digital files through Stripe Checkout and a user-owned delivery page. The hard boundary is buyer familiarity, payment operations, tax handling, discovery, and creator workflow, plus payments, tax, distribution, and operations.
coreLoopDIY: Sell a small catalog of digital files through Stripe Checkout, deliver purchased files from a delivery page, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront.
whatYouLose: buyer familiarity, payment operations, tax handling, discovery, and creator workflow
ongoingBurden: checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Gumroad because creators pay to outsource the dangerous and tedious parts around money, delivery, tax, and customer access. The recurring cost buys checkout, webhooks, tax, refunds, fraud, entitlements, storage, email, accessibility, backups, and customer support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Medusa
priorArt.desc: Active open-source commerce platform with modular checkout and fulfillment primitives.

alternatives.name: CourseLit
alternatives.desc: Digital downloads, sales pages and payments in one compose file; mail and media still need adult supervision.

facts.install: Docker Compose, with SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL set before first start
facts.dataFormat: Application records in MongoDB; production media uploads use MediaLit plus S3-compatible object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: CourseLit trades Gumroad's instant hosted checkout and delivery for a heavier self-hosted stack with mail and object-storage setup.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker starts the app, but a production setup also needs SMTP for email login and MediaLit/S3-compatible storage for uploads

alternatives.name: Easy Digital Downloads
alternatives.desc: WordPress with a checkout and download locker; good at files, not interested in being your creator empire.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Hosted digital products and file delivery on a permanent free plan; generous limits, distinctly funnel-shaped furniture.

facts.dataFormat: Contacts, funnels, course/community content, orders, emails and uploaded files in systeme.io's vendor-managed cloud; the underlying storage format is not published
facts.gapVsPaid: systeme.io is more funnel-shaped and less frictionless for a few standalone creator products than Gumroad.
facts.setupBlocker: Selling requires connecting a payment gateway; the free plan is capped at 2,000 contacts, three funnels, one course, one community and one custom domain

alternatives.name: Vvveb
alternatives.desc: A visual storefront with digital delivery and licence files built in; the server is the subscription.

facts.install: Download and upload the PHP release, open the site URL, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Content, products, orders and settings in MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite or PostgreSQL; media and downloadable files on the server filesystem
facts.gapVsPaid: Vvveb replaces Gumroad's nearly instant creator checkout and delivery with a full store that the seller must operate.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable files, mail and payment configuration, plus ongoing server updates

alternatives.name: WooCommerce
alternatives.desc: Sells and delivers downloads without platform rent; the recurring charge is maintaining WordPress.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FOSSBilling
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It does downloads and billing, but the project still labels itself beta and warns about rough edges and limited support.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A commerce framework with no ready-made creator storefront or file-delivery experience for non-builders.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Polar
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Open source on paper, but the usable hosted product takes 5% plus 50 cents per sale and self-hosting is a developer project.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Platform fee plan and a single-creator storefront DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Gumroad in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, Stripe Checkout, and S3-compatible storage; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: sell a small catalog of digital files through Stripe Checkout, deliver purchased files from a delivery page, and manage customers from a user-owned storefront.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement products, variants, prices, files or lessons, coupons, customers, orders, and entitlements.
Use Stripe-hosted Checkout and verify every webhook signature and idempotency key.
Grant access only after confirmed payment and revoke it on refund or chargeback.
Create a customer library with signed short-lived download or lesson URLs.
Add order search, resend receipt, refund handoff, export, and an immutable event log.
Document taxes as the creator's responsibility and do not calculate unsupported jurisdictions.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out merchant-of-record tax remittance.
Deliberately leave out a buyer marketplace or affiliate network.
Deliberately leave out advanced communities, certificates, mobile apps, and enterprise learning features.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
